description: We are a team of curious and passionate technology enthusiasts participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in exploring real-world problems through software development, data analysis, artificial intelligence, and creative problem-solving. Our goal is to build an innovative, practical solution using NASA's open data and collaborate with people who are passionate about technology, science, and space exploration.
summary: CrewPulse is a simulated astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to help identify changes in crew health during space missions. It provides an interactive dashboard to monitor heart rate, body temperature, sleep duration, and a wellness score across mission days. The system establishes an individual baseline and compares later readings against it to flag unusual changes as normal, warning, or critical signals. Visual trend charts help users understand how health indicators change over time. CrewPulse was developed in response to the challenge of supporting astronaut health during long-duration missions, where early awareness of potential health changes is important. The prototype uses clearly labelled simulated data and NASA research resources to inform its design. It is an educational demonstration, not a clinical diagnostic system or a live NASA telemetry platform.
details:
CrewPulse is an interactive astronaut health monitoring prototype developed for the challenge “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions.”

The dashboard allows users to select one of two simulated astronauts and explore health indicators over a 30-day mission timeline. It displays heart rate, body temperature, sleep duration, and a wellness score through metric cards and interactive trend charts.

The system establishes a personal reference baseline using the first five mission days. It compares later readings against that baseline and identifies changes using configurable prototype rules. For example, it flags a heart-rate change of 10% or more, a temperature change of 0.5°C or more, a sleep decrease of at least one hour, or a wellness-score decrease of 10 points or more. Signals are grouped into normal, warning, and critical levels to make unusual patterns easier to notice.

The intended benefit is to demonstrate how continuous monitoring, personal baselines, and visual trend analysis could support awareness of astronaut health during long-duration missions. The prototype is designed as an early decision-support concept, not as a medical device or a replacement for professional assessment.

Technology used: Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, and Plotly. The project was developed in Visual Studio Code and deployed using Streamlit Community Cloud. The source code and simulated dataset are available in our public GitHub repository.

NASA's Life Sciences Data Portal and its Spaceflight Standard Measures research, including the Sleep Quality/Team Questionnaire, were consulted to inform the project's sleep and crew-wellness context. These NASA datasets were not directly downloaded or integrated into the prototype. All astronaut readings in the dashboard are synthetic simulated data created for demonstration purposes. The heart-rate, temperature, and wellness indicators are illustrative and are not validated medical thresholds. ChatGPT assisted with planning, coding, debugging and documentation.
